title: This Snake Spits Venom Into Your Eyes From 8 Feet Away

scenes.text: This snake spits venom into your eyes from eight feet away.
The spitting cobra hits at least one eye eight times out of ten. Some species, every time.
The burst lasts 50 milliseconds. Too fast to correct, so it can't afford to miss.
scenes.keywords: cobra fangs open mouth slow motion

scenes.text: It doesn't aim at your eyes. It predicts where they'll be a fifth of a second later.
Then it shakes its head mid-spit to spread the spray wider.
In the eyes, the venom burns and can blind. From eight feet. Don't blink.

description:
Spitting cobras squirt venom at the eyes of a threat from up to about 8 feet away. In tests, black-necked spitting cobras hit at least one eye 8 times out of 10, and Mozambique spitting cobras hit every time.
The spray lasts only about 50 milliseconds, so the snake tracks your head movement and aims where your eyes will be about 200 milliseconds later, shaking its head to widen the spray. The venom causes burning pain and can cause blindness.
Which snake scares you most? Comment below.
first_comment: Spitting cobras only spit at moving faces. In the Bonn study they ignored moving hands and barely reacted to photos. Would you freeze or run if one reared up in front of you?
